Ethereum's intrinsic economics is rebuilding itself in motion with tech bugs and the macroeconomic picture overlaying each other in the span of 48 hours. The week wraps up for a major alternative crypto project with a sudden Glamsterdam hard fork stop after testnet launch revealed a dangerous bug in the fee recalculating mechanism, brutally breaking the logic in smart contracts.

As the Ethereum community debated the ability of the network to sustain on old power, Vitalik Buterin showed up with a manifesto which completely zeroes out all the panic around mainnet's decreasing revenue. The "red line" behind Vitalik's updated vision is that the community should stop being fixated on the idea of ETH as "fee-burninng token". For a basic blockchain layer worth $270 billion, attempts to build evaluation on the amount of gas burned are a dead end. For Vitalik, the novel of "ETH as store of value (SoV)" is much more viable amid all the global uncertainty around.

This U-turn, taken by a key visionary of the ecosystem, happened at $2,240 for ETH and may drastically change all the plans developed with a focus on Glamsterdam architecture. The hard fork was initially projected for the logic of blockspace surplus, not the deficit. Ecosystem builders are already readying expansion of L1 capacity with the help of EIP-8037 (tariffs calibration) and EIP-7928 (parallel production) with an aim to raise gas limits up to 200 million units. The logic is that the excess of free space will cheapen the transactions, while token burning rates will gradually be cut.

The market saw a risk of deflation in this concept. Vitalik took a front-step. By his estimates, the historical peaks of burning through EIP-1559 "never were as strong as they seemed". They were dependent on inner cyclical activity of crypto speculations. And it itself was falling once every bear market started.

EIP-1559 is not going anywhere, and Vitalik openly says "don't be sad" if the volume of gas burned will forever stay below the 10% mark. The source of value for Ethereum lies in completely another dimension.

Solana's co-founder, Anatoly Yakovenko, unexpectedly aligned with Buterin on this matter. "You can't focus on fees as the products", he said, calling such an idea "absolutely meaningless". According to Yakovenko, the blockchain network must generate real value for the end users, not control the price of getting into the block.

Vitalik is absolutely right that you can’t focus on fees as the product. That’s absolutely meaningless. You need to pick a product, the thing that brings value to people, and do that really well.

There is lots of technical stuff and philosophy around, but what the missed deadline on the testnet and Vitalik's manifesto reveal is that Ethereum opts for long-term, secure, and even a bit boring stability of the basic layer. Infra doesn't try to flirt with the market through deflationary records.

#5262. Forget ‘Ultrasound Money’? Vitalik Buterin Pushes New Ethereum Store-of-Value Vision

Ethereum co-creator Vitalik Buterin is challenging one of Ether’s most celebrated investment narratives, suggesting that the second-largest crypto’s long-term value should depend less on how many tokens the network burns and more on its ability to become a reliable store of value.

The remarks could signal a major shift in how Ethereum’s value proposition is presented, particularly as declining transaction-fee burns weaken the deflationary narrative that once made ETH attractive to investors.

In a Sunday morning post on X, Buterin outlined three main reasons for shifting attention away from Ethereum’s fee-burning narrative and toward its potential as a store of value.

First, he argued that ETH’s deflationary appeal was never as powerful as it seemed. Although the 2021 EIP-1559 upgrade introduced a mechanism to burn a portion of transaction fees, the amount of ETH destroyed has not always been enough to offset new token issuance. In his view, making fee burns the central measure of Ethereum’s success places too much emphasis on a single aspect of its token economics. According to Buterin, even if fee burns remain below 10% of the level required to offset new issuance indefinitely, Buterin said, “we should not feel sad,” adding that “the value of ETH comes from elsewhere.”

Another concern is that prioritizing ETH as a fee-burning asset could push Ethereum toward decisions that undermine its core principles. Buterin suggested that designing the network primarily to maximize transaction-fee burns could create tensions with decentralization and censorship resistance. Such an approach could require trade-offs that make the network less open and less resistant to external control, potentially weakening the very qualities that distinguish Ethereum from competing blockchain networks.

Notably, the fee-burning mechanism was central to Ethereum’s popular “ultrasound money” narrative, which gained significant traction among ETH investors during the 2021 bull run. The thesis suggested that by permanently removing a portion of transaction fees from circulation, Ethereum could become increasingly deflationary, potentially making ETH scarcer and more valuable over time.

He also sees an opportunity in the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence. As AI continues to disrupt industries and reshape economic activity, dependable financial infrastructure could become more valuable. “In the era of AI disruption, stability will be highly valued,” he wrote.

Buterin believes Ethereum’s emphasis on stability could give ETH a stronger store-of-value proposition in this changing environment, shifting the investment narrative away from token burns and toward the network’s ability to preserve trust over the long term.

Interestingly, Buterin’s position also found support from Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko, who appeared to share his skepticism about making transaction fees the centerpiece of a blockchain’s value proposition. Yakovenko dismissed the idea of treating fees as the product, calling it “absolutely meaningless.” He argued that blockchain networks should focus on delivering tangible value to users rather than trying to control how much people pay to have their transactions included in a block.

#5261. Flare CEO Pushes Back Against XRP 'FUD'

Flare CEO Hugo Philion has expressed his frustration about recent fear, uncertainty, and doubt (FUD) around XRP and reiterated that the future of the cryptocurrency should not be centered solely around Ripple.

The Flare CEO recently addressed in an X post the constant habit of XRP holders to evaluate the future of the cryptocurrency through the prism of what Ripple is doing and what it isn't.

"The value and narrative of XRP should never have been viewed as being dependent on the actions of a single actor," the Flare CEO said.

The Flare CEO emphasized that XRP holders should instead concentrate their efforts on finding ways to improve the usability of the cryptocurrency.

In this context, Philion said that XRP holders need to consider three main questions.

The first question is what XRP holders are actually doing to utilize their XRP holdings. The second is how they can convince potential investors to hold XRP.

Finally, the third point that the Flare CEO mentioned is that the XRP community should find a way to transform XRP from a predominantly speculative asset into usable capital.

"And that's part of the reason we created Flare because we feel like there's always been more that can and should be done with XRP," the Flare CEO added.

Besides, the Flare CEO also invited XRP holders to try Flare. According to Philion, it's a way to make XRP less dependent on Ripple.

The Flare CEO's statements come amid increasing frustration around XRP and the lackluster performance of the cryptocurrency.

Over the past year, the price of XRP has gone down by around 50%, and at press time, the price of the cryptocurrency stands at $1.16.

Recently, Ripple's former chief technology officer David Schwartz also faced some criticism over the poor performance of XRP. Schwartz noted that his influence on the XRP price was very limited.

One X user raised a question about whether FLR holders are doing enough to demonstrate the value of the cryptocurrency, especially when it's possible for XRP holders to use Flare's decentralized finance ecosystem without purchasing FLR.

Still, Philion dismissed the claim that there is no need for FLR when using FXRP (a tokenized version of XRP on Flare).

"It's incorrect btw that you can use FXRP without needing FLR," the Flare CEO clarified.

According to Philion, what Flare Smart Accounts do is simply abstract away the need to manage FLR and make the experience more convenient. At the same time, FLR is used to pay transaction fees on the underlying networks.

Besides, the Flare CEO also underlined that in the long term, there should be more use cases for the token apart from transaction fees.

"Usage is important. Need to get fee generation going in a broader way in the ecosystem," he added.

#5259. Bitcoin Falls Below $76,000 as Chip Stocks Crash and Liquidations Hit $1 Billion: Why Is Crypto Down Today?

Why is crypto down today? A chip-stock crash sent Bitcoin below $76K, wiped out $1B in longs and pulled $430M from Bitcoin ETFs.

Short answer to “why is crypto down today?” Bitcoin fell 6% to below $76,000 after a Wall Street chip-stock crash on Thursday, November 5, wiped out $1.03 billion in leveraged bets and pulled $430 million out of Bitcoin ETFs. The selling hasn’t stopped overnight.

Bitcoin traded at about $75,700 on Binance on Friday morning, down from $80,547 at the start of Thursday. Ethereum lost 8.2% to $2,218, XRP fell 9.7% to $1.18 and Solana dropped 6.9% to $89.22. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell to 28, in “Fear”, from a neutral 50 a day earlier.

The trigger came from stocks. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed down 12.2%, its members Nvidia and AMD lost 9.3% and 17.3%, and the Nasdaq fell 5.5%. Crypto stocks went with them: Strategy dropped 9.3% and Coinbase 9.7%.

So what turned a tech sell-off into a crypto crash, and where can Bitcoin find a floor?

Today was a 4σ day for equities. The S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq fell 5.5%, a decline seen roughly once every 19 months. Bitcoin fell about 5%. $STRC closed at $99.56, just 44 cents below par.

— Michael Saylor (@saylor) November 5, 2026

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

Wall Street opened at 14:30 UTC, and Bitcoin broke within the hour. The 15:00 UTC candle on Binance fell from $78,288 to $75,568, the day’s busiest hour with $513 million traded.

Yahoo Finance’s market coverage linked the stock rout to the Democrats’ clear midterm win and what it could mean for AI infrastructure spending and its regulation. Chipmakers, the biggest winners of the AI trade, took the hardest hit.

Leverage did the rest. CoinGlass counted $1.03 billion in liquidations over 24 hours, positions closed by force when margin ran out. Longs made up $924.94 million of that, or 89.4%, across 199,365 traders.

Bitcoin longs lost $255.88 million and Ether longs $163.83 million. The biggest single wipeout was a $10.94 million ETHUSDT position on Binance.

DISCOVER: Trump Media Moves $344 Million in Bitcoin to Crypto.com as TRUMP Hits a Record Low

US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $430.2 million in net outflows on Thursday, and not one of the 12 funds took in money. SoSoValue’s ETF tracker shows Fidelity’s FBTC led with $199.87 million out, ahead of BlackRock’s IBIT at $104.97 million.

Grayscale’s GBTC lost $49.90 million, Franklin Templeton’s EZBC $32.92 million, VanEck’s HODL $23.64 million and ARKB $18.90 million.

It undid Wednesday in one session. Funds had added $74.6 million on November 4, the only inflow day so far this month. November’s first four trading days now add up to $869.8 million in outflows, on top of $515.9 million that left in October.

Fidelity’s turn is the detail to watch. FBTC took in $236.7 million on Wednesday while IBIT bled, then gave back most of it a day later.

Bitcoin closed Thursday at $76,088, just under its 200-day EMA at $76,536. That average had held as support through the October pullback.

The 50-day EMA at $79,822 now sits above the price, and the $81,971 high from before last week’s Binance hack is the next resistance beyond it.

On the downside, the $74,968 swing low is the first support. Below it, the 50% Fibonacci retracement of the July-to-September rally sits at $72,598.

One caveat: funding rates on Bitcoin perpetuals are still slightly positive on OKX, so longs haven’t fully cleared out even after a billion-dollar flush.

For anyone still asking “why is crypto down today?”, the answer runs through Nasdaq. If chip stocks steady when New York opens on Friday, Bitcoin has a shot at reclaiming its 200-day average. If they don’t, $74,968 is the line between a bad day and a deeper correction.

Anthropic is targeting a valuation of up to $1.02 trillion, based on its proposed IPO price range of $70–$80 per share.

The company could raise $69.4 billion through its public offering and another $26 billion through a private placement.

Nvidia and Alphabet are each committing $10 billion, highlighting the financial exposure of major technology companies to Anthropic's growth.

Anthropic’s planned IPO is emerging as a major test for the AI industry, with the Claude developer targeting a valuation of approximately $1 trillion. Backed by Nvidia and other technology companies, the offering could raise more than $90 billion through public and private share sales. Its market debut comes as investors increasingly scrutinise the cost of developing artificial intelligence and the returns on infrastructure spending. Can Anthropic justify its ambitious valuation, and what could its listing mean for Nvidia and other AI stocks?

Anthropic has proposed selling 865 million shares at $70–$80 apiece, potentially raising up to $69.4 billion. Based on outstanding shares, the upper end of the range implies a valuation of approximately $1.02 trillion. Including options and other potential shares, the fully diluted valuation could reach around $1.4 trillion.

Anthropic is seeking to raise up to $69.3B in its IPO, below earlier expectations of $80B-$100B, Reuters reports.It plans to sell 866.7M new shares at $70-$80 each, with all proceeds going to the company.Trading could begin next week on Nasdaq under $ANT. pic.twitter.com/HoF0ENA2T6

The company is also arranging a separate $26 billion private placement involving Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC. Google and Nvidia are each committing approximately $10 billion, making them the largest participants in the arrangement.

Anthropic plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. The offering’s final price and trading date remain subject to the IPO process.

Nvidia’s $10 billion commitment to Anthropic highlights its growing financial exposure to the AI ecosystem. The company already benefits from demand for GPUs used to train and operate advanced AI models. Anthropic’s expansion could support further demand for computing capacity, particularly as enterprise adoption of Claude increases.

However, the investment also raises questions about interconnected financing in the AI industry. Nvidia is investing in a company that needs substantial computing infrastructure, including its own products. Investors will therefore examine whether AI infrastructure spending is generating sustainable customer demand and revenue rather than depending heavily on capital flowing between industry participants.

Anthropic’s growth has been accompanied by substantial infrastructure commitments. Its latest filing disclosed approximately $17 billion in third-quarter revenue and $33.2 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026. However, the company also reported a nine-month net loss of $104 billion and computing and infrastructure commitments of approximately $900.9 billion.

The figures highlight the financial challenge facing advanced AI developers. Revenue growth remains important, but investors will increasingly assess operating costs, capital requirements and the path towards profitability.

Anthropic’s public listing could provide an important indication of how much investors are willing to pay for large-scale AI businesses. Strong demand could support confidence across the technology sector, while a weaker reception could renew concerns about elevated AI valuations.

For Nvidia and its technology partners, the central question is whether the enormous investment in AI infrastructure can translate into sustainable returns. Anthropic’s IPO will put that question directly before public-market investors.

Alta, a financial infrastructure company building the foundation for the next generation of global finance, has announced $80 million in total funding — including a $47.5 million Series A round and $32.5 million in previous seed financing. The Series A was led by Index Ventures, with participation from GV (Google Ventures), Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg, and Capital 49.

The timing is deliberate. Alta’s launch comes as regulatory clarity improves and institutional demand for tokenized finance accelerates.

Today’s global financial system remains fragmented and riddled with inefficiency. Moving money across borders can take days, and institutions must hold substantial cash buffers to maintain liquidity across jurisdictions and payment networks. Globally, an estimated $4 trillion sits tied up in prefunded accounts.

Alta is building a more efficient alternative — combining instant settlement with global payment connectivity, foreign exchange, and treasury management in a single system.

At the core of Alta’s technology is a new blockchain architecture built on recursive zero-knowledge cryptography. It allows institutions to keep balances, transactions, identities, and compliance policies private — while still cryptographically proving that every transaction meets the required rules.

Designed to operate across assets, chains, and jurisdictions, Alta pairs programmable compliance with the controls and scalability that institutional finance and agentic commerce demand.

Leading financial platform Airwallex has chosen to build on Alta, connecting its global payments infrastructure with Alta’s blockchain technology. Beyond pay-ins and pay-outs via stablecoins, the collaboration will support connectivity to local fiat payment networks across 200 countries and 90 currencies.

That reflects Alta’s broader positioning: neutral infrastructure that banks, payment providers, and other financial institutions can all build on.

Alta’s first product is designed to help businesses manage liquidity more efficiently and free up the cash buffers trapped in prefunded accounts. Built on tokenized assets, it enables just-in-time funding and more efficient foreign exchange — and lets businesses move instantly in and out of yield-bearing tokenized assets, maximizing the interest earned on otherwise idle capital.

“With the rise of agentic banking and programmable payments, stablecoins are becoming an important vector for settlement. Financial institutions need blockchain infrastructure that is private, neutral, regulated, and connected to global fiat rails. Alta is building exactly that,” said Jack Zhang, Co-Founder of Alta and Co-Founder/CEO of Airwallex. “We’re proud to be an early design partner and help Alta deliver onchain finance at institutional scale.”

Alta’s investors bring together expertise across financial technology, enterprise infrastructure, and blockchain innovation.

“Loong is the sort of technologist you only meet a few times in a career. After a major fintech exit from his first company, he went on to run the largest supercomputing calculation in history at its time, then discovered a cancer drug now in human trials. With Catherine’s exceptional track record of bringing industry leaders to the table and Jack’s understanding of the problem space, this is a team we had to back,” said Jan Hammer, Partner at Index Ventures.

“The Alta founders have successfully built and scaled multi-billion-dollar technology and financial infrastructure businesses, and understand how to de-risk complex institutional execution. We have been impressed with their combination of deep-tech blockchain engineering, institutional go-to-market knowledge, and vision for scale, and we look forward to supporting them in their mission to reimagine financial infrastructure at its core,” said Tom Hulme, Managing Partner at GV.

The new funding will support continued development of Alta’s blockchain infrastructure, the expansion of its institutional partnerships and global financial connectivity, and the growth of its engineering and compliance teams.

Bitcoin snapped a seven-week holding above the 50-week moving average (MA) with a weekly close at $74,968. According to the latest Galaxy Research report, BTC settled 0.7% under this key line, which now sits at $75,488.

Alex Thorn, the firm’s head of research, calls it a fakeout. The history is on his side: it's standard Bitcoin mechanics to slip back under the 50-week MA right after a bear-market bottom, and it's what shapes the structure of the four-year cycle. It has happened exactly twice before.

Losing the trendline again right after reclaiming it is how the biggest cryptocurrency has always behaved. Previous cycles played out like this:

The current chart is running the same script. From the $123,524 peak in October 2025, the coin bled 51.8% into the June cycle bottom at $59,517. A rebound then shoved the price back above the 50-week MA at $81,195. Today’s price is 7.7% off that September reclaim level, yet Bitcoin maintains a comfortable 26% cushion above the June bottom.

Thorn isn’t selling certainty. Two cycles is a thin sample, and bottoms only get confirmed in the rearview mirror. The margin for error is wide: in 2012, Bitcoin broke down again from 18% above the line, while in 2015 it held from just 8% above.

“Bitcoin just closed below its 50 week moving average after holding above it for 7 consecutive weeks. Two other times (2011-12 & 2019-20) btc closed below its 50w after reclaiming its post-bear bottom. Neither of those times did the bear make a new lower low (weekly close data),” the analyst notes.

One level kills the bull case for this 4-year cycle: $59,517. Galaxy Research says on-chain metrics, whale positioning and market sentiment all point to a consolidation that is technically ripe for stacking on spot. The technical case stays alive as long as Bitcoin reclaims the 50-week MA and holds it within the next month.

#5246. XRP Ledger Unveils Fee-Free Quantum-Proof Upgrade as Ripple Races Toward 2028 Security Deadline: Here’s What’s Coming

The XRP Ledger is preparing for a major security overhaul as quantum computing moves from a theoretical concern to a growing priority for the crypto industry. With Ripple targeting 2028 for its post-quantum security transition, developers are now unveiling a proposed quantum-resistant upgrade that promises to protect users against future attacks without introducing additional transaction fees.

The development could mark a significant turning point for the network, raising questions about what exactly is changing, how the upgrade will work, and whether XRP holders will need to do anything before the looming security deadline.

The XRP community has a new development to watch as the XRP Ledger Foundation outlines plans to strengthen the network against future quantum computing risks. The proposed upgrade would introduce quantum-resistant accounts, giving users an additional layer of protection against emerging cryptographic threats while keeping transaction costs unchanged.

Although the feature has yet to be implemented, the proposed upgrade would allow XRP Ledger users to register NIST-approved ML-DSA-44 quantum-resistant signing keys and deactivate their existing authentication keys. This would give accounts an additional layer of protection against potential quantum computing attacks, particularly those whose public keys have already been exposed on the network.

Importantly, users could adopt the enhanced security system without changing how they store, hold, or access their XRP. The concern stems from how transactions are authorized on the network. When users sign transactions through their cryptocurrency wallets, their public keys can become exposed, potentially creating an attack vector if sufficiently advanced quantum computers emerge.

Such technology could eventually undermine existing cryptographic protections, putting accounts with exposed public keys at risk. The XRP Ledger Foundation’s proposed solution is designed to address this vulnerability before quantum computing advances to the point where such attacks become practically achievable.

Beyond the additional protection, the proposal has another notable selling point: affordability. Users would not have to pay higher transaction fees to benefit from the enhanced security. In other words, XRP holders could strengthen their accounts against emerging quantum threats without incurring additional transaction costs, making the proposed upgrade particularly appealing to the community.

Although the upgrade has not yet gone live, the team has outlined its next steps, with a migration study planned for the first half of 2027. The research will explore how existing XRPL accounts can move to the new quantum-resistant security framework, including the transition process and what account holders would need to do to adopt the upgraded protection.

Developers are also addressing discrepancies in how the proposed system generates cryptographic keys across its Python, JavaScript, and server implementations, a necessary step toward ensuring consistent and reliable performance across the network.

As ZyCrypto previously reported, Ripple has outlined a comprehensive four-phase roadmap to make the XRP Ledger, its decentralized Layer-1 blockchain, resistant to potential quantum computing attacks, with full quantum readiness targeted for 2028.

You do not need to run validator nodes or manage external DeFi wallets. Unlike bank deposits, exchange savings programs generate yield through principal-protected Simple Earn pools, margin lending, Real-World-Asset (RWA) instruments, and fixed-rate loans. Comparing flexible vs fixed terms, VIP rate boosters, Proof of Reserves, and Auto-Earn idle-balance sweeps helps you pick the right account across Binance, OKX, BloFin, Bybit, Kraken, and Bitget.

Crypto savings accounts on centralized exchanges are not bank deposits. They are not covered by government deposit insurance such as FDIC or FSCS protection. Savers face exchange custodial counterparty risk and borrower utilization fluctuations on flexible lending pools. Fixed Simple Earn plans also lock principal until maturity, and BTC, ETH, and SOL balances carry market price volatility.

A traditional bank savings account holds fiat currency insured up to statutory limits (such as $250,000 FDIC coverage in the United States). It lends deposits through regulated banking channels. A crypto savings account (such as Simple Earn on Binance, OKX, BloFin, or Bitget, or Easy Earn on Bybit) holds digital assets like USDT, USDC, BTC, and ETH under exchange custody without government deposit insurance.

BloFin Simple Earn lists principal-protected savings plans across 10 featured digital assets. RWUSD is BloFin Earn’s flexible Real-World-Asset (RWA) yield product, paying a published 3.68% APR on a flexible duration. Unlike peer-to-peer margin lending pools whose rates swing hourly with trader leverage demand, RWUSD provides a steady dollar-referenced yield stream with anytime subscription and redemption.

BloFin VIP 1 (unlocked at 50,000 USDT in assets with zero platform token requirement) offers 7-day VIP Fixed Simple Earn rates of 4.80% APR on USDT, 3.00% on USDC, 3.20% on SOL, 3.20% on ETH, 0.80% on XRP, and 0.40% to 1.60% on 14/60-day VIP BTC. By comparison, Bitget’s published VIP Simple Earn rates pay 4.00% APR on USDT, 2.28% on USDC, and 0.15% on BTC.

Fixed-term Simple Earn contracts lock your deposited tokens until the scheduled settlement date in exchange for a guaranteed fixed APR. On BloFin Simple Earn Fixed plans (which run from 2 to 180 days depending on the coin), early redemption is not supported, so savers who want instant liquidity should use Simple Earn Flexible, RWUSD (3.68% APR), or Flexible Onchain Earn.

#5243. Bitcoin Slides to $73,510 Over the Weekend: Did Nvidia Scandal Trigger BTC’s $2,000 Flash Crash?

Bitcoin news: BTC fell to $73,510 on Sunday, 100 minutes after the Nvidia scandal broke. Thin weekend trading let the drop run further.

In Bitcoin news overnight, BTC USD price fell from $75,607 to $73,510 in ten minutes on Sunday evening, its lowest price since August 21. The worst of it came at 21:55 UTC, or 4:55 p.m. in New York. In that single minute, Bitcoin dropped 1.9% on Binance.

Most traders blamed Nvidia. Earlier that afternoon, CNBC reported that Nvidia’s board had opened an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman U.S. intelligence agencies believe was passing information to Beijing (it’s just speculation for now).

Huang admitted the affair in an email to staff.

After Jensen Huang admitted having an affair, a whale opened a 10x short on 30,000 $NVDA ($5.44M) on Hyperliquid.https://t.co/RztJx5FNge pic.twitter.com/zuyV2K0ftN

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 9, 2026

The bounce since then has been small. BTC traded at $74,184 on Binance on Monday morning, 2.2% below where it stood when the Nvidia story broke. The drop also marked a fifth straight losing week: the weekly candle closed at $74,851, below the week’s open of $78,354.

So did the Nvidia scandal really trigger the dump, or did thin weekend trading turn an ordinary sell-off into a sharp one?

Discover: Sam Altman ChatGPT AI Predicts an Insane Move for Cardano (ADA)

The timing does not fit a straight reaction to the news. CNBC published its report at 3:12 p.m. Eastern time on Sunday, which is 20:12 UTC. Bitcoin traded at $75,880 on Binance in that minute. For the next 90 minutes, almost nothing happened. At 21:44 UTC, BTC sat at $75,607, just 0.4% lower than when the story appeared.

Then the selling started, and it started in Ethereum. Between 21:50 and 21:55 UTC, ETH fell 6.9% on Binance, from $2,213 to $2,060. Bitcoin fell 2.4% over the same five minutes.

That pattern points to a liquidation cascade, a chain of forced sales. Traders who borrow to bet on higher prices get their positions force-closed when the price falls past a set point. Each forced sale pushes the price down to the next group of bets.

BREAKING: $1,000,000,000 liquidated from the crypto market in the past 10 minutes.$BTC falls under $74,000$ETH falls under $2,125$XRP falls under $1.10 $SOL falls under $90 pic.twitter.com/hIZhzQFJJe

— Watcher.Guru (@WatcherGuru) November 8, 2026

The news still mattered. Nvidia is the biggest AI stock, and Bitcoin has traded in step with AI shares for weeks: Thursday’s chip-stock sell-off is what pushed BTC below its 200-day average. With stock markets closed, crypto was the only market open to sell into the headline.

A second headline added to the Bitcoin news mood. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called Iran’s demands “outrageous” and said talks had made no progress.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

Weekend trading explains why the drop went so far. Over the past year, about $24 million of BTC changed hands on Binance in a typical weekend hour, half the $48 million in a typical weekday hour.

We checked every hour in that year in which Bitcoin fell at least 2.5% below the hour’s opening price. There were 29 of them.

Sunday’s drop came with $180 million of trading in the hour. That is the second-lowest of all 29, and about half the median of $366 million.

In other words, it took less selling than usual to move the price this far. The busiest minute, 21:55 UTC, traded $75 million of BTC on Binance, about three times what changes hands in a whole weekend hour.

Weekends do not cause more crashes, though. Only 6 of the 29 drops came on a Saturday or Sunday, slightly fewer than the 29% of all hours that fall on weekends. What a quiet weekend changes is how far the price moves for each dollar sold.

One note: much of the forced selling happens in futures markets, which this count does not include.

So both played a part. Nvidia and Iran gave traders a reason to cut risk, and thin weekend trading let the selling run further than it would on a weekday.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

It held on the first test. BTC bounced to $75,735 within two hours of the low, but it has slipped back to $74,184, and the daily chart still leans lower.

Bitcoin trades below all three of its daily exponential moving averages (EMAs), trend lines that give recent prices more weight. It lost the 200-day EMA, which tracks the long-term trend, on Thursday.

For traders following Bitcoin news this week, Monday’s stock market open is the next test. It is the first chance for Nvidia shares to trade on the news, eight days before the company reports earnings on November 17.

XRP Ledger co-creator David Schwartz dropped his $1.7 million tax bill on X to settle a long-running fight over the token’s value. Ripple’s CTO Emeritus was swatting away haters who accused him of dumping XRP on the market. One commenter called XRP “a terrible investment,” adding that nobody would blame the engineer for heading for the exit. Schwartz kept it short: “The $1.7 million I paid in capital gains tax says otherwise.”

In 2025, Schwartz sold about 2.5 million XRP, according to his own words. Nearly all of it came from bonuses for his work in 2020 and 2023. Posting the numbers was no accident. Schwartz is killing rumors about what Ripple’s "big guns" really pocket and proving he has nothing to hide.

The sale is one chapter in a bigger personal saga Schwartz has been unpacking piece by piece from 2024 through 2026. At his peak he held around 26 million XRP. By August 2026, that stack had shrunk to just 2 million. Describing the 92% drawdown, he chose his words carefully: “I think I’m down from about 26 million at my peak to about 2 million now.”

Some went out as gifts and transfers, but he sold most of it on the open market.

He started taking profits the moment the price touched $0.10. Schwartz admits he never believed the coin would break $0.25. The same paranoia made him dump his entire 40,000 ETH position at a measly $1.05 apiece.

“Obviously, I wish I hadn’t done those things,” the developer says of the billions he left on the table.

Schwartz opposes the approach many attribute to as "diamond hands". He openly says he “really, really hates risk” and doesn’t count himself among long-term holders. He and his wife had an ironclad rule to sell a fixed slice of their holdings every time the price printed a new all-time high. Cashing out is simply the cost of being able to “sleep better at night.” These days, volatility barely touches him as his net worth is now largely cut loose from price swings.

Based on his own admission, Schwartz moved most of his savings into Ripple stock. The shares are illiquid, sure, but they give direct exposure to the tech giant’s wins and fully insulate his personal capital from exchange chaos.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Zcash has set a new high in its network hashrate just days after the NU7 upgrade, which slashed block times by a third to 25 seconds. Zcash activated its NU7 upgrade on November 6, 2026, at block 3,543,405.

Zcash network hashrate: 32.62 GSol/s, up 5.8% in 30 days. ⛏️ An all-time high. https://t.co/1vNROBAvd2

Zcash hashrate refers to the total computing power of all miners on the ZEC network. It is calculated by the current network difficulty, the average block find time set by the cryptocurrency network and/or the effective block find time of the latest blocks.

ZEC got 3x faster following the NU7 upgrade, which launched on November 6, with block times down from 75 to 25 seconds, and the Sprout pool retired, marking a new era for Zcash.

Faster blocks mean more room for shielded transactions. NU7 adds per-block limits: 330 Orchard or Ironwood actions, 300 Sapling inputs and outputs, a shared budget of 330 across pools, and no new Sprout JoinSplits. These limits more than double Orchard protocol throughput while reducing the worst-case sync load a spammer can push onto light wallets by about 37%.

NU7 does not raise Zcash's fixed 21 million cap; halvings will now come every 5,040,000 blocks instead of 1,680,000, so the issuance schedule holds at roughly four years per halving. NU7 also starts allocating funds for future mining rewards. Some 60% of aggregate transaction fees will flow into a public reserve that pays later mining rewards.

In what comes next after the NU7 upgrade, Zcash developers have proposed cutting block times in a potential NU7.1 upgrade just days after NU7 went live. The proposal would reduce target block times from 25 to 20 seconds, aiming to speed up transaction confirmations and improve user experience and network latency.

A Geth developer has proposed a fix to the client's gas estimation, according to draft pull request #36084 on GitHub. The patch addresses an issue in the current estimator, which could result in incorrect gas limits due to failed internal calls (calls from one smart contract to another) being ignored.

Although the transaction could still be completed, there is no evidence that the action the user wanted has actually happened.

The issue lies in a mechanism where a smart contract calls another smart contract, catches an error, and then proceeds to a refund, records the failure, or skips an item entirely. Technically, the transaction was successful, but the outcome is different for the user.

This could potentially result in wallets suggesting a gas limit that is enough to finish the transaction, but not enough to complete the work inside it. The developer also noted that EIP-8037 could make this behavior more common, since gas returned from failed internal execution can help fund the fallback.

According to the pull request, the change includes a stricter definition of success for gas estimates. This version of Geth would improve the way it deals with internal failures, counting failed internal calls and contract creations instead of checking only whether the transaction completes.

Even if the transaction completes, the estimate would get rejected if it produces more internal failures than a reference execution with a higher gas limit.

Nonetheless, the developer stressed that an internal call that always fails should not push the estimate higher indefinitely. The reference execution enables the estimator to keep existing failures without allowing additional ones caused by insufficient gas. The proposal also introduces a separate Amsterdam reference, preventing unnecessary increases made purely to access the state gas reservoir.

The developer states that they've replayed 432 mainnet transactions with the new set of rules from the Amsterdam update and that the suggested change fixed 64 out of 67 cases.

The gas limit increased by 4%. 254 additional estimates were unaffected due to the lack of the problem, with 3 cases being undetected.

For regular investors, the proposed change should improve the reliability of wallet estimates and reduce transactions that complete without delivering the intended result, despite introducing higher gas limits in some cases. Luckily, there is no proven link between higher gas limits and higher fees.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Cardano (ADA) has entered epoch 666, yet another milestone for the blockchain, which has been live since its launch in September 2017.

The number has drawn attention for its connection to the biblical 666, but the development also points to the Cardano network's basic timekeeping and staking mechanism.

Popular Cardano blockchain explorer Cexplorer displays that epoch 666 started on Nov. 5, 2026, and is expected to end on Nov. 10, with 1 day and 10 hours left to close. The milestone marks another five-day cycle finished in Cardano's long-running proof-of-stake system.

Cardano divides its operation into epochs, which are five days long and consist of 432,000 one-second slots. The importance of epoch 666 is largely symbolic and not technical, as it does not coincide with any major protocol upgrades or hard forks. But the number 666 has merely provided an interesting talking point for the Cardano community.

In a separate milestone, the Cardano network has processed over 127,000,000 transactions on mainnet. According to Cexplorer data, Cardano has recorded a total of 127,203,164 transactions.

In upgrade news, DijkstraNet, the Dijkstra hard fork testnet, has been hard forked to protocol version 12 and is now available for testing and integration against the full Dijkstra feature set, with the exception of Linear Leios.

Node 11.2 was pre-released on October 28 and successfully used to transition DijkstraNet into the Dijkstra era, and DB Sync 13.8.0.0 was released for all networks.

In separate upgrade news, Midnight has completed its upgrade from Ledger 8 to Ledger 9, bringing new capabilities for developers alongside security, compatibility, and performance improvements across the network.

Ledger 9 introduces native support for widely used cryptographic standards including ECDSA and Keccak-256, expands wallet and custody compatibility, and enables contracts to interact directly with one another.

Keccak-256 is the standard algorithm that Ethereum uses to scramble data into fixed-length cryptographic fingerprints. ECDSA is the standard digital signature method that networks like Bitcoin and Ethereum use to prove ownership of a specific wallet address.

#5222. “Tired After 7 Years”: Why This Veteran XRP Investor Considers Selling Everything at Current Prices

XRP’s potential run to $10 may not be enough to keep every longtime holder invested. In a striking admission, a long-time XRP investor has revealed plans to sell his entire position at current prices, despite the token’s much-anticipated upside target. The comments have sparked fresh debate over whether years of waiting will ultimately pay off for XRP holders or whether some are ready to walk away before the next parabolic rally.

In a recent post on X, Genfinity founder Ryan Solomon, known as King Solomon, expressed growing frustration with XRP after holding onto the cryptocurrency for seven years. Despite the community’s long-standing hopes of a major explosion toward $10, he suggested he may no longer be willing to wait for that milestone, revealing plans to sell his entire XRP position at current market prices and citing the significant opportunity cost of staying invested so long.

“When XRP eventually hits $10, many won’t sell,” Solomon said. “I’m likely selling everything at current prices. Tired after 7 years. Too much opportunity cost,” Solomon wrote.

He also expressed frustration with what he described as shifting narratives and gaslighting surrounding XRP. After years of waiting, he seems increasingly unconvinced that continuing to hold the payments-focused token is worth sacrificing other investment opportunities.

The comments carry added weight given Solomon’s years of involvement in researching XRP and the broader digital-asset infrastructure sector through Genfinity. His willingness to consider walking away after seven years suggests that even the prospect of XRP eventually reaching the much-coveted $10 level may no longer be enough to keep some longtime holders committed.

In simple words, his stance highlights the frustration that can build even among long-term participants in the XRP ecosystem. That sentiment comes as XRP hovers around $1.10, according to CoinGecko data, marking a decline of approximately 51% over the past year and highlighting a prolonged downturn that is testing investors’ patience.

Another longtime XRP community member going by the name Nikolas echoed Solomon’s frustration, admitting that holding out for the $5-$10 price range was one of his biggest investment mistakes. He also criticized the XRP community for what he described as a growing inability to think critically, suggesting that many holders have become too attached to bullish expectations.

The investor further questioned the relationship between Ripple Labs and XRP, arguing that the company’s business interests appear increasingly disconnected from the token’s performance. In his view, Ripple may be prioritizing its corporate growth and investors while XRP holders struggle to see comparable benefits from the company’s expansion.

Meanwhile, crypto commentator Good Evening Crypto suggested that Solomon’s concerns may reflect a much broader sentiment among longtime XRP holders. He said a friend working in private equity, who has held XRP since 2021, recently expressed similar frustrations about the opportunity cost of staying invested.

Although Good Evening Crypto said he does not share the same view, he acknowledged that Solomon’s decision to consider selling deserves attention given his experience and standing in the community. He suggested that thousands of other XRP holders may be quietly reaching the same conclusion but have yet to voice their frustrations publicly.

Together, these comments point to growing discontent among some longtime XRP holders, raising questions about whether the token’s anticipated upside still justifies the years of waiting.

Telegram CEO Pavel Durov has shared new metrics on the Gram wallet integration in the messenger.

According to Durov, over the last 48 hours alone, users activated more than 700,000 non-custodial Gram wallets.

The screenshot shared by the Telegram CEO shows more than 329,000 new addresses a day. According to GRAM documentation, a wallet is created automatically when a user receives their first token transfer.

700K+ self-custodial wallets created on Telegram in the last 48 hours alone. Adoption spreads virally: a wallet activates the moment someone receives Grams. The crypto revolution is going strong. https://t.co/JPO2KVMip0

The growth comes after a series of changes Telegram made to the TON network earlier this year under Durov's "Make TON Great Again" campaign.

Back in 2020, Durov was forced to kill the original Telegram Open Network project and return more than $1.2 billion to investors after a lawsuit from the US SEC.

Community developers kept the open-source code alive as The Open Network (Toncoin).

This year, Telegram became the largest validator of the network. Besides, Telegram cut TON fees sixfold.

In June, the token was renamed back to its original name, Gram, after a community vote, with 81% of voters in favor. In July, Durov announced that Telegram would integrate a native non-custodial Gram wallet into every Telegram app.

The Telegram CEO described it as "the largest deployment of a non-custodial crypto wallet in history" and promised instant zero-fee transactions for more than 1 billion Telegram users.

According to TON developer Andrew Rogozov, the custodial Wallet in Telegram will stay separate from the new wallet. Now, onboarding happens natively within standard chat windows.

Still, while wallet creation metrics break records, liquidity inside the network is lagging behind with total value locked at $42.01 million, according to DefiLlama.

These hundreds of thousands of new addresses are mostly making microtransactions, such as buying Telegram Premium, paying for in-app ads, or settling small P2P transfers.

Besides, Telegram's validator weight is raising centralization concerns among industry critics. At the same time, the native wallet is still unavailable for US users.

At press time, Gram is trading at $1.05. The token is still more than 87% below its 2024 high of $8.25.

"The crypto revolution is going strong," Durov said.

#5219. Bitcoin CPI Reaction: 10 of 13 Cool Inflation Reports Triggered an Hourly Gain – Can Inflation Data Reverse the Downtrend?

Bitcoin CPI reaction: October CPI lands at 8:30 a.m. ET, core seen at 0.22%. Cool prints lifted BTC in the first hour 10 times out of 13.

The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes October’s consumer price index (CPI) on Tuesday, November 10, at 8:30 a.m. in New York, or 13:30 UTC. The Bitcoin CPI reaction that follows could set the tone for the week. The CPI is the main U.S. measure of inflation, and it will shape the Federal Reserve’s next rate decision.

Economists expect core prices, which leave out food and energy, to have risen about 0.22% in the month. That would be a slowdown from September’s 0.33%.

Economists expect growth in the core CPI to have moderated in October to around 0.22%, though the full range of estimates is broad enough to round down to 0.1% or round up to 0.3%.

Due to the government shutdown in Oct 2025, there's no tidy year-earlier figure. pic.twitter.com/CFM7ikw8fO

— Nick Timiraos (@NickTimiraos) November 9, 2026

Bitcoin trades near $74,400, still close to Sunday’s two-month low of $73,510.

CPI days move crypto. We checked Bitcoin’s first hour after the last 24 releases. When core inflation came in at 0.2% or lower, BTC rose in that hour 10 times out of 13. When it came in at 0.3% or higher, it rose only 4 times out of 10.

So which way will today’s number push Bitcoin?

The forecasts point to a calmer month. Seventeen banks and research firms surveyed by The Wall Street Journal see a median rise of 0.25% for headline CPI and 0.22% for core. Journal reporter Nick Timiraos posted the table on X.

That spread matters. The government reports CPI rounded to one decimal place. With forecasts this spread out, the core reading could print anywhere from 0.1% to 0.3%. A 0.3% would match September’s pace and read as inflation that is not cooling.

The yearly comparison will also be messy. The government shutdown in October 2025 meant no CPI was published for that month, so there is no clean year-over-year figure.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

This is the last CPI report the Federal Reserve will see before its December 8-9 meeting. Traders already expect a rate hike: on Tuesday morning, Polymarket gives an 86.5% chance of a 0.25-point increase and 11.5% for no change.

Higher rates tend to weigh on Bitcoin. They make cash and bonds pay more, which pulls money away from assets that pay no interest, like crypto.

A cool reading could shave those odds and give Bitcoin room to bounce. A hot one would lock in the hike.

DISCOVER: Fed Meeting Today: Traders Price a 95% Hold and a 79% December Hike. What Does It Mean for Crypto?

We measured the Bitcoin CPI reaction on Binance. We took the 24 CPI reports published since October 2024 and measured Bitcoin’s move in the hour after each 8:30 a.m. release.

The pattern is a lean, not a rule. The biggest drop came on February 12, 2025, when core rose 0.4% and BTC lost 1.9% in an hour. Last month’s 0.3% reading cost it 1.4%.

So far it has. BTC trades at $74,398 on Binance, about 1.2% above Sunday’s low.

On the daily chart, Bitcoin sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that weight recent prices more. The 200-day EMA is at $76,481 and the 50-day EMA at $79,128.

For anyone tracking the Bitcoin CPI reaction, the first hour after 8:30 a.m. is the one to watch. In 20 of the last 24 reports, Bitcoin ended the next 24 hours moving in the same direction as in that first hour.

#5216. Schiff: Saylor's STRC Is 'Dead'

Earlier today, gold bug Peter Schiff claimed that Strategy executive chairman Michael Saylor was trying to prop up the floundering investment product by carrying out heavy stock buybacks.

"Michael, STRC is dead. You have been keeping it alive on artificial life support with your buybacks," he wrote.

According to Schiff, Strategy is running out of money to prop up its preferred stock. The ongoing Bitcoin market crash is going to aggravate the situation even further, he argued.

"But you're running out of cash. And the selling pressure on STRC will increase as Bitcoin crashes," Schiff wrote.

The Bitcoin bear went on to criticize the generous 12% annualized dividend yield of STRC, saying that ultimately the yield wouldn't be enough to cover the risks of the product.

"It won't be nearly enough yield to cover the risk. 12%," he warned.

The stern comments from Schiff followed a typical bullish tweet from Saylor. In his post, Saylor claimed that AI could not mint new Bitcoin.

"AI can make me rap. It can't print Bitcoin," the cofounder of Strategy wrote.

Strategy's Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Stretch Preferred Stock (STRC) seeks to provide regular dividend income to investors while trading near its $100 face value.

Currently, STRC offers a 12% annual dividend yield, which Strategy has been working to keep steady in order to keep the stock trading near its face value.

However, maintaining the price stability of STRC has come at a big cost.

In its Q3 financial results on Oct. 29, Strategy reported that the firm had spent a total of $2.04 billion on repurchases of STRC as of Oct. 25.

Describing the heavy buybacks as a success, the firm said it had successfully put STRC on the road to financial recovery.

However, these buybacks have come under fire from Schiff, who questions whether the firm can keep propping up investor demand by repurchasing its shares forever.

In spite of the bearish comments from Schiff, Strategy isn't budging on its strategy of ramping up its Bitcoin holdings.

The firm's recent regulatory filing shows that Strategy bought another 1,036 BTC between Nov. 2 and Nov. 8.

The total cost of these purchases is estimated to be $81.9 million, with an average purchase price of $79,012 per BTC.

With the latest purchase, Strategy now holds an eye-watering 850,364 BTC.

#5215. Bybit Says $17.3B Proof of Reserves Covers 50 Assets, but the Audit Has Limits

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Bybit says the latest snapshot of its proof-of-reserves system covered $17.3 billion in customer assets across 50 cryptocurrencies. The exchange's November 3 announcement describes its 41st report, with figures independently checked by security firm Hacken against an October 27 snapshot.

Bybit says the latest snapshot of its proof-of-reserves system covered $17.3 billion in customer assets across 50 cryptocurrencies. The exchange's November 3 announcement describes its 41st report, with figures independently checked by security firm Hacken against an October 27 snapshot. The exercise offers a view of assets and customer balances at a specific moment, but it should not be mistaken for an all-purpose guarantee that an exchange could meet every liability under every scenario.

Bybit says its reserve ratios exceeded 100% across all 50 covered assets, including 112% for USDT, 405% for USDC, 102% for Bitcoin and 101% for Ether. Those percentages compare identified reserves with customer balances under the stated methodology. An unusually high ratio for one token does not mean the business has the same excess in every asset or that reserves could be freely moved between customer pools. Readers should also distinguish a token-by-token reserve ratio from consolidated corporate solvency, which incorporates obligations that may not appear in a proof-of-reserves snapshot.

The release identifies the audit point as October 27 at 06:00 UTC. Reserve balances, withdrawals, borrowing, market prices and off-exchange exposures may have changed after that time. The value of recurring disclosures lies partly in their comparability: users can look for persistent gaps or unexpected movements rather than treating a single publication as permanent reassurance. Bybit says the checks covered the 50 listed crypto assets, but the exact perimeter, included customer categories and handling of institutional arrangements are questions worth reviewing in the detailed report.

The exchange says Hacken carried out the verification. Third-party involvement is useful, particularly when the reviewer explains its methods and limitations, but the word 'audit' can be interpreted too broadly. A Merkle-tree exercise may allow customers to verify that a balance was included while proving possession of identified onchain assets. It does not, by itself, necessarily establish that there are no undisclosed debts, encumbrances, affiliated-party claims or operational weaknesses. The scope of work therefore deserves as much attention as the name of the verifier.

Asset backing is a fundamental question for custodial exchanges because users depend on the firm to return assets they cannot directly control. Yet security controls, market surveillance, legal ownership of customer property, segregation practices and withdrawal resilience also matter. A fully funded snapshot is only one component of a broader risk picture. The report can be especially informative when combined with clear explanations of liabilities, independent financial statements where available and timely incident reporting. It should not substitute for personal decisions about custodial concentration.

Bybit users can inspect the methodology and verify balances if the relevant tool supports that check. External analysts should compare successive reports and look for consistency between claimed assets and observable onchain holdings. Markets benefit from more systematic disclosures, but transparent limitations are an important part of credible transparency. The milestone is the reporting process, not a declaration that counterparty risk has disappeared.

#5214. XRP Price Plunges to $1.05 After a Hot CPI Report: Will the Support Stand?

Ripple XRP fell to $1.05 after a hot CPI report. After 7 of the last 10 hot reports, XRP was higher a day later. Can $1.05 hold?

Ripple XRP fell to $1.05 on Tuesday within five minutes of the U.S. October consumer price index (CPI) report, which showed XRP USD price rising faster than economists expected.

XRP crypto traded at $1.0797 when the report came out at 8:30 a.m. in New York, or 13:30 UTC. By 13:35 UTC it had touched $1.0500 on Binance, a 2.8% drop and its lowest price since August 19. It has since bounced to about $1.07. Bitcoin fell with it, dropping to $73,525 in the same five minutes.

The drop puts XRP back on a level it has tested before. Between late June and mid-August, XRP traded around $1.05 for weeks. The level held the first time and broke the second.

So will the support stand this time, and what do the CPI numbers tell us?

BREAKING: October CPI inflation rises +0.4% month-over-month, above expectations of +0.3%.

Core CPI inflation rose +0.3%, also above expectations of +0.2%.

BLS will not be releasing year-over-year figures due to the October 2025 government shutdown.

— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) November 10, 2026

Prices rose faster than forecast in October. The Bureau of Labor Statistics said consumer prices rose 0.4% in the month, against the 0.3% economists expected.

Core prices, which leave out food and energy because they swing the most, rose 0.3%. The forecast was 0.2%. Core inflation has now run at about 0.3% for three months in a row.

The report is missing one usual figure. The bureau did not publish a yearly inflation rate because it never collected prices in October 2025, during the government shutdown. That leaves the monthly numbers to carry the whole report.

Those monthly numbers matter for the Federal Reserve. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech this morning that he already leans toward a 0.25 percentage point rate hike in December. If core CPI came in around 0.3% again, he said, a 0.5 point hike “should be considered”.

Core CPI did come in at 0.3%. Before the release, traders saw almost no chance of a hike that large. Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more, which tends to pull money out of risky assets like XRP.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

The first move after a hot report has often faded. We measured XRP’s price on Binance in the 24 hours after each of the last 24 CPI reports, from October 2024 to October 2026.

Ten of those reports had core inflation of 0.3% or higher, like today’s. After seven of them, XRP was higher 24 hours later. The median move was a 1.4% gain.

The record is weaker this year. Of the four hot reports in 2026, XRP was higher a day later only twice. After the last one, on October 14, it fell 4.4% in 24 hours.

The difference this time is the Fed. A hot report that only confirms a small hike is easier for traders to shrug off. One that puts a larger hike on the table, as Waller laid out, gives sellers more to work with.

EXPLORE: XRP Price Forecast: Ripple at Risk of Losing Key Support, $1 Next?

The level has a history this year. XRP has spent two long stretches around $1.05 since June.

Today’s low of $1.0500 sits right on that zone. The first test of a level often holds. Each new test tends to leave fewer buyers there.

XRP trades at about $1.07 on Binance after the CPI drop, down 2.8% in 24 hours and 17% in a week. It is 71% below its July 2025 record of $3.65.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, XRP sits well below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA stands at $1.294 and the 200-day EMA at $1.350.

For Ripple XRP, the first test of $1.05 has held so far. The daily close decides it: a close above $1.05 keeps the support alive, while a close below it opens the way to $1.

Based on his market observation, the analyst noted that since the recently concluded 2026 midterm elections, U.S. stock markets have surged around 12% while Bitcoin dropped by 4.6%. Over the same period, gold and silver prices have risen by 5% and 7%, respectively.

#5212. North Korean Hackers Flip Stolen Binance Funds Into NEAR Meme Coins

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

North Korea's TraderTraitor group has started laundering funds stolen from Binance through newly created meme tokens, according to Elliptic.

The $6.4 billion Binance hack took place in October 2026 and was attributed to TraderTraitor.

According to Elliptic, the hackers have used this technique on Tron and NEAR, while a similar approach has appeared on Solana.

Between Nov. 5 and 7, 2026, the hackers launched at least six of these tokens on NEAR: FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI and SINU. Launching one cost around 25 NEAR (about $90).

According to Elliptic, the hackers paired each token with NEAR in a liquidity pool on a decentralized exchange (DEX). Wallets holding stolen NEAR deposited it into the pool and received the new token. A second set of wallets then sold the token back into the pool and withdrew NEAR.

This way, the funds never move directly from the wallets holding stolen assets to the receiving wallets.

According to Elliptic, the receiving wallets look like ordinary traders who sold a token at a profit.

Each token got typical meme branding, from monkeys to an image of Elon Musk under an "Elon 2028 President" banner. Elliptic noted that Musk is not linked to the tokens.

Each token was sold for the first time less than three hours after launch, and at least 75% of its trading took place within one day. None of the six tokens has traded since Nov. 8, and the creators of four of them withdrew the remaining liquidity on that day.

In total, 117,000 NEAR (about $421,000) moved through the scheme. Most of it then went into stablecoins or to a cross-chain bridge.

Elliptic noted that five of the six token creators received funds from a wallet that had been selling the previous token 2 to 13 minutes before the new launch, and in this way the operation funded itself.

The only outside activity was a few small purchases of FUK on its first day, which accounted for less than 1% of its volume, Elliptic said.

According to Elliptic, the on-chain trail stays public, and the technique makes tracing the funds slower. The hackers can also create many tokens and abandon each one after use.

In 2025, after the Bybit hack, the same scheme moved at least $24 million through Tron. In that case, the hackers paired a worthless token with a stablecoin.

In the Binance case, Elliptic identified a similar token on Tron on Nov. 2. On Nov. 3, stolen SOL was swapped into existing thinly traded tokens on Solana and then sold for USDC.

Elliptic said that so far only a small part of the stolen funds has gone through meme tokens. About 11.8 million NEAR from the theft has not moved yet, and at press time, NEAR is trading at $3.60, which puts these funds at around $42.4 million.

Elliptic also advises compliance teams to check funds coming from liquidity pools, especially pools with newly created tokens.

"Laundering is a race to move funds before they are flagged," Elliptic added.

TL;DR: Solana's November 5 developer changelog highlights a collection of tooling and validator improvements rather than one headline-grabbing network upgrade. Among them are faster builds for JavaScript applications, changes affecting validator operations and further work around execution tools.

Solana's November 5 developer changelog highlights a collection of tooling and validator improvements rather than one headline-grabbing network upgrade. Among them are faster builds for JavaScript applications, changes affecting validator operations and further work around execution tools. For developers, these smaller improvements can influence how quickly applications ship and how reliably infrastructure behaves. For investors, the distinction is that a published development update is not necessarily a newly activated change on mainnet.

One item in the changelog concerns the JavaScript SDK build process using Rolldown. The developers describe a reduction in an internal build benchmark from around two seconds to almost zero. That is a promising productivity claim, but it applies to the specified workflow and benchmark rather than every Solana app suddenly loading faster for users. Faster library builds can improve testing and release cycles, particularly for teams maintaining many packages. Its end-user effect depends on whether downstream developers adopt the updated tools and whether the gains carry over to their own projects.

The update also points to work on the Agave validator client, typed interfaces and elements of Firedancer leader handover. These terms describe software and operational changes within the infrastructure that keeps the chain running. Their practical significance lies in reliability, interoperability and the conditions under which different validator implementations coordinate. However, a changelog reference should not be treated as evidence that every validator has deployed the work or that a planned network feature has passed all activation checks. Operators need specific release notes, configuration guidance and rollout schedules.

The changelog includes improvements involving Anchor, RPC-related tools and local development environments such as Surfpool. Anchor is widely used for building Solana programs, while RPC services provide the interface through which wallets, apps and analytics products query the chain. Small optimizations in account allocation or local testing can save developer time and reduce avoidable mistakes. They do not remove the need for security review, careful transaction handling or capacity planning. Because Solana applications rely on several layers, a weakness at the RPC or front-end level can still affect users even when core consensus works normally.

Solana has long emphasized throughput and latency, but engineering benchmarks depend on hardware, software versions and the specific task measured. An SDK build benchmark is not a transaction-per-second statistic, while validator handover work is not a promise of zero outages. Keeping those categories separate helps readers understand what the team has actually improved. Adoption may eventually show up in developer retention, easier deployment and more dependable applications, but those effects take time and should be measured rather than assumed from a release note.

Developers can follow the linked repositories, testing results and future rollout notices for each change. The clearest evidence of impact would be adoption in major tools, reproducible performance measurements and fewer operational headaches for app builders and node operators. The November update reflects continuous ecosystem maintenance—often less dramatic than a large protocol announcement, but essential to whether Solana can support more demanding financial applications over time.

#5208. Circle Makes the Case for AI Agent Payments, With Spending Controls at the Center

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Circle is arguing that stablecoins could become a useful payment layer for AI agents that buy software, access services or settle transactions on behalf of people and businesses. A November 4 explainer from the USDC issuer sets out what it calls agentic commerce, a concept that would allow authorized software to initiate purchases within predefined rules.

Circle is arguing that stablecoins could become a useful payment layer for AI agents that buy software, access services or settle transactions on behalf of people and businesses. A November 4 explainer from the USDC issuer sets out what it calls agentic commerce, a concept that would allow authorized software to initiate purchases within predefined rules. It is a vision for a developing market, not evidence that an autonomous AI payments network has already reached mass adoption.

The basic idea is to let a software agent complete a purchase after receiving instructions and permission from a human or business. An agent might compare pricing, obtain a computing service, pay a provider and record the transaction without asking a person to click through each step. This differs from a chatbot that only recommends products or from an automatic recurring subscription. Stablecoins are appealing in this setting because value can move over internet-native rails and settle across borders, but those features are useful only when an agent can prove what it is authorized to do.

The central design challenge is delegated authority. A business needs to specify which agent may spend, how much, on which categories of supplier and for what period. It also needs authentication, records of the instruction that triggered a payment and a way to revoke authority. Without those safeguards, automated payments can turn minor software errors or malicious prompts into real financial losses. Circle's discussion points to the infrastructure opportunity, but a stablecoin transfer alone cannot determine whether the underlying purchase was legitimate or met the user's expectations.

USDC and other dollar-linked tokens could allow small cross-border payments and programmable transfers that are difficult to reproduce with traditional card infrastructure. However, blockchain transfers can be difficult to reverse. Conventional card payments often involve dispute rights, fraud monitoring and customer-support processes that do not automatically accompany an onchain transfer. A workable agent payment service therefore needs explicit handling for refunds, incorrect goods, failed delivery and disputes. It must also address sanctions checks, identity requirements and jurisdictional limits where relevant. Technology that moves money quickly cannot replace those business obligations.

Developers are experimenting with AI systems that interact with tools, APIs and online marketplaces. As those systems gain the ability to perform tasks rather than simply produce text, a reliable method of paying for digital services becomes more relevant. Stablecoin issuers and payment processors see potential demand, but practical uptake depends on merchants accepting the method and users trusting the controls. The most credible demonstrations will involve narrow, verifiable use cases rather than broad claims that intelligent agents can safely manage unlimited funds.

Payment providers will need to show who bears liability when an agent makes a mistaken purchase, how permissions are audited and how customers recover from fraud. They will also need to show cost advantages after fees, compliance and integration work are included. Circle's essay is best read as an articulation of a developing architecture, not a new product launch. The long-term test is whether automated payments become easier for ordinary businesses without making financial control harder.

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Valour, a subsidiary of DeFi Technologies, says it has added eight digital asset exchange-traded products to Sweden's Spotlight Stock Market. The November 5 announcement expands the issuer's range beyond the most established cryptocurrencies into a mixture of decentralized finance, blockchain infrastructure and speculative community tokens.

Valour, a subsidiary of DeFi Technologies, says it has added eight digital asset exchange-traded products to Sweden's Spotlight Stock Market. The November 5 announcement expands the issuer's range beyond the most established cryptocurrencies into a mixture of decentralized finance, blockchain infrastructure and speculative community tokens. The listings widen the menu available through a securities-market wrapper, but the variety also makes it important for investors to understand what each product actually tracks.

Valour's new SEK-denominated products reference Venice Token (VVV), Canton Coin (CC), Raydium (RAY), Morpho (MORPHO), Maple (SYRUP), Pump.fun (PUMP), Dogwifhat (WIF) and Bonk (BONK). They represent very different markets. Some connect to lending, trading or institutional blockchain networks, while others derive demand from online communities and token speculation. Presenting all eight as one diversified crypto strategy would be misleading. A buyer of one listed product is exposed to its specific token and to the terms of the ETP, not to a balanced basket of the eight assets.

An exchange-traded product can give eligible investors exposure through a brokerage account rather than requiring them to maintain a wallet and manage token transfers. That can simplify record keeping and access within markets where the product is available. It does not necessarily provide the same legal structure or protections as a conventional equity fund, however. Investors should review whether the product is physically backed, how custody is handled, what fees are charged, and whether creation and redemption work efficiently. The securities wrapper can reduce some operational burdens while leaving underlying crypto price risk very much intact.

Canton and Morpho are associated with institutional blockchain and DeFi infrastructure, Raydium with Solana-based trading and Maple with onchain credit. By contrast, meme-linked tokens such as Dogwifhat and Bonk have historically depended heavily on market sentiment. Pump.fun exposure carries its own commercial and regulatory questions. None of these classifications determines future performance, but the differences matter for portfolio construction and due diligence. The existence of a regulated trading venue for an ETP is not an official endorsement of the underlying token's economic value.

The products are quoted in SEK, so an investor whose reference currency is different must consider exchange-rate moves as well as the token price. Trading hours and liquidity may also differ from around-the-clock cryptocurrency markets. That mismatch can create wider spreads or price gaps when significant token moves occur while the securities venue is closed. Buyers should examine the issuer's market-making arrangements and the gap between quoted prices and indicative net asset values rather than assuming that an exchange listing always guarantees a tight execution price.

Valour's expansion shows how issuers are testing demand for more specialized crypto exposures through familiar financial channels. Whether the new products become meaningful investment options will depend on trading volumes, spreads, fees, custody disclosures and sustained interest beyond launch week. For market observers, the story is less about eight fresh tickers than the effort to package increasingly niche digital assets for traditional securities accounts—and the safeguards needed when investors follow them there.
